title: Morning Digest, Saturday 7 November 2026
intro: The Sweden Democrats drop their demand for cabinet seats and the Centre Party asks both blocs for a full plan, the AI sell-off hits Asia, Belgium's king refuses De Wever's resignation, Israel's opposition lines up behind Eisenkot, and OpenAI releases its first model rated 'Critical' for cyber capability.

items.title: The AI sell-off spreads to Asia; Wall Street steadies
items.body: On Friday Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi each fell about 6 percent and SK Hynix 10 percent after Thursday's US rout. In New York the Nasdaq then rose 1.1 percent and Nvidia nearly 3 percent, though all three main indexes ended the week down. A strong US jobs report (165,000 new jobs against about 59,000 expected; unemployment 4.1 percent) led traders to raise the odds of a December interest-rate rise by the Federal Reserve.
items.source: Reuters via Business Standard; Finimize; HNGN, 6-7 Nov

items.title: Belgium's king refuses De Wever's resignation
items.body: After meeting the five coalition leaders, King Philippe sent the prime minister back to the negotiating table on the 2027 budget, with a report due on 16 November. The parties are split over whether to raise taxes on the wealthiest, and a stopgap monthly budget will probably be needed in January.

items.title: Israel's opposition backs Eisenkot for prime minister
items.body: In consultations with President Herzog, 67 of 120 Knesset members recommended Gadi Eisenkot, including both Arab-led parties and Lieberman's Yisrael Beiteinu, against 46 for Netanyahu. Herzog names his candidate on Sunday; Netanyahu, who stays on as caretaker, questions the result, while the election committee says the vote was sound.
items.source: Sunday Guardian; Haaretz; The Hill, 5-6 Nov

items.title: Trump's cabinet under strain after the midterms
items.body: Republican Thomas Massie says he will force a House vote next week on impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth over the Iran war unless he resigns; several Republicans expect it to pass, and Trump backs Hegseth. Separately, Bloomberg reported that Secretary of State Rubio is weighing leaving; the State Department called it a 'baseless hoax'.
items.source: Forbes; Gray News via KGNS; Just Security; Yahoo News, 5-6 Nov

items.title: Hackers also tampered with French blood-bank freezers
items.body: Attackers took over cold-room controls at a refrigeration supplier to France's blood service, pushing set temperatures to extreme levels at three sites; alarms caught it and no blood products were lost. No one has claimed it, and no link to the recent supermarket freezer attacks has been established.

items.title: California empties its death row
items.body: Governor Newsom commuted the sentences of all 548 people on death row to life without parole.

items.title: SD drops its demand for cabinet seats; C asks M and S for a full plan
items.body: Jimmie Åkesson said on Friday that the Sweden Democrats will no longer insist on ministers and would accept Kristersson leading a four-party centre-right government without them, setting no counter-demands. The Centre Party replied that it could govern with any party except those on the fringes, and gave Kristersson and Magdalena Andersson until next Friday to present a complete programme with policy, funding and delivery: Kristersson must show how SD would be kept from dictating terms, Andersson how she would govern without the Left Party. Kristersson called both moves welcome, and the Speaker gave him a few more days beyond Tuesday's deadline.

items.title: Border checks extended, now citing Russia
items.body: Targeted checks at Sweden's internal Schengen borders will run from 12 November to 11 May. The government now names sabotage and hybrid attacks linked to Russia's war as the reason; May's decision cited crime and terrorism.

items.title: Funding
bullets: Sellpy (Michael Arnör) — second-hand clothing platform — about 167 million kronor at a 5.5 billion valuation — H&M (majority owner) and senior staff.
Norrsken Evolve — impact investor backing early-stage founders — closes a fund of nearly 700 million kronor, more than planned.

items.title: Scheduled
bullets: Sunday 8 November: Herzog names who gets the first chance to form Israel's government.
9-10 November: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris.
From Monday 9 November: possible House vote on impeaching Hegseth.
Tuesday 10 November: Israel's new Knesset is sworn in; US October inflation figures.
10-11 November: US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.
Thursday 12 November: the caretaker government presents its budget; Sweden's extended border checks begin; UK third-quarter GDP.
Friday 13 November: the Centre Party's deadline for M and S to present their government plans; Kristersson reports to the Speaker around then.
items.source: HNGN; Rio Times; Finimize; SVT; earlier editions

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber, its first model rated 'Critical'
items.body: The hacking-focused model, the highest risk level in OpenAI's own framework, goes only to vetted customers of its offensive-security programme. OpenAI says it found 81 new high-severity Firefox flaws, now being patched by Mozilla, and solves 48.5 percent of a standard exploit-writing test against 32.1 percent for its predecessor.

items.title: Baidu publishes ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base weights
items.body: A 280-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model (14 billion active per token) trained on 33.5 trillion tokens, released before any instruction tuning so developers can adapt it; Baidu says it matches DeepSeek V4 Flash and MiMo V2.5 at similar size, with no independent scores yet.

items.title: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck
items.body: Musk says production in Texas winds down around mid-2027 to free capacity for the Cybercab robotaxi. Sales were about 20,000 last year, against his original forecast of 250,000 a year, and fell another 28 percent this year.
items.source: AP via NBC New York, 6 Nov

items.title: Google takes over Crusoe's Wyoming data-centre site
items.body: A day after announcing a 17-billion-dollar investment in the project, Google bought the site from Crusoe, a company that builds and rents out AI data centres, which had struggled to sign customers for it.

items.title: Research pulse
bullets: VFlash (NVIDIA, Johns Hopkins): robot and driving models output plans as boxes and trajectories one coordinate at a time; VFlash predicts each whole shape in one pass, cutting decoding time by about 80 percent while making 3D trajectories more accurate (arXiv 2611.08449, top of both Hugging Face and alphaXiv).

Understanding AI from the Inside (Oxford, Mila, EleutherAI and others, with Bengio and Biderman): a book-length survey of mechanistic interpretability that argues the assumption that understanding models' internals makes them safer is largely untested, and calls evaluation standards the field's most pressing gap (arXiv 2611.08438).

BestRand (Bosch Research, CMU): scoring a model on a small random slice of a benchmark usually lands close to its full score, but because models fail on similar items an unlucky slice can be far off; drawing many random slices and keeping the one where a few probe models score as they do on the full set halves the risk of large errors across more than 70 benchmarks (arXiv 2611.00883, Hugging Face papers).
items.source: arXiv via alphaXiv; Hugging Face daily papers, 31 Oct-5 Nov
